name: WP Remove Category from Archive Title
author: Isrg Rajan

sections.description:
WP Remove Category from Archive Title removes default archive title prefixes such as “Category:”, “Tag:”, “Author:”, date prefixes and custom taxonomy labels. It supports WordPress 5.5+ and PHP 7.4+.

Prefixes are removed by default after activation, with no setup step. Optional settings let you keep prefixes for selected archive types.

sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin from the WordPress plugin directory, or upload the wp-remove-category-from-archive-title folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen.
  3. Visit Settings > Archive Titles if you want to keep prefixes for specific archive types.
sections.faq:
Does this work with custom taxonomies and post formats?

Yes. Custom taxonomy archives and post format archives use the same core prefix filter, so their prefixes are removed by default.

Does it work with Elementor or other page builders?

Elementor core’s Archive Title widget uses WordPress archive titles, so it normally inherits the change. Third-party builder widgets may render titles independently; if a prefix remains, use the builder’s own title setting or hide it with CSS. This plugin does not hook undocumented builder filters.

What about titles that contain a colon?

Only the exact prefix supplied by WordPress is removed. A title such as “News: Updates” is left intact after the “Category:” prefix is removed.

Can I restore prefixes for some archives?

Yes. Go to Settings > Archive Titles and uncheck the archive types where you want to keep the prefix.

Are there developer filters?

Yes. wprcat_remove_prefix_for_context controls prefix removal per context, and wprcat_archive_title filters the final title.

Does the plugin add anything to the front end?

No. It only changes archive titles and adds an admin settings page. There are no scripts, tracking, ads or front-end credit links.
